summary: M13 save commits as one atomic revision-fenced SettingsScope.mutate instead of sequential set/unset (Issue #69). buildMutation (pure model) converts staged writes into one ordered op list; the card calls props.scope.mutate(ops, snapshot.revision) exactly once, clears dirty/stagedClear only after the mutation settles, and keeps the draft on throw. The scope type now comes from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings/client (0.1.2-rc.1 contract, which exposes mutate); the previously pinned dsh-client-runtime rc.2 type lacked it.
steps: Verified at 5a1b6e1: save looped await scope.set/unset per field (partial writes could persist if write 3 of 5 failed) and never used snapshot.revision as a fence.

The client contract with mutate exists only in @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings 0.1.2-rc.1 (the runtime surface the card actually binds to), so the type import moved there; dsh-client-runtime rc.2 has no mutate and stays a peer.

Per the issue's API correction note, SettingsScopeController.mutate may recover instead of rejecting on Host conflict; the card keeps its draft on a thrown failure and re-syncs from the mirror otherwise.
limitations: Component-level save behavior is not covered (no React test harness in the repo); the tested boundary is buildMutation. Host-side conflict recovery may silently reload host state; the editor re-syncs from the mirror.
